---
title: "Install and verify the software"
---

Install the tools in this order: R, RStudio Desktop, Git, then your GitHub
account. Restart RStudio after installing or updating Git.

## R

Download R from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org) and choose the installer for
your operating system. After installation, open RStudio and run this in the
Console:

```r
R.version.string
```

You should see an R version rather than an error.

## RStudio Desktop and Quarto

Install the free desktop version from [Posit](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
RStudio includes Quarto, so no separate Quarto installation is normally
required. In RStudio's Terminal, verify it with:

```bash
quarto --version
```

## Git

Install Git from [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/downloads). In RStudio's
Terminal, run:

```bash
git --version
```

Then record the name that should appear on your commits:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "YOUR_GITHUB_EMAIL"
```

Use an email recognized by your GitHub account or the private `noreply` address
shown in GitHub's email settings. These commands configure authorship; they do
not sign you into GitHub.

## GitHub account

Create an account at [github.com](https://github.com). Choose a professional
username you are comfortable using for course work and send that username - not
your password - to the instructor. Verify the account's email address so that
repository invitations and workflow notifications arrive.

## A local course folder

Create a parent folder such as:

```text
macOS:   /Users/avery/Documents/POLI210
Windows: C:/Users/Avery/Documents/POLI210
```

Avoid a folder managed by Dropbox, iCloud Drive, OneDrive, or a network drive.
Cloud-sync software can lock, duplicate, or make files inside Git's hidden
`.git` directory online-only.
